questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of quantitative data?
options: Brands of cars in a parking lot
Weights of bears at a zoo
Types of flowers at a florist
Jersey numbers on a basketball team
hints: Which one can you meaningfully average?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Weights are numerical measurements, so they are quantitative data.

questions.prompt: Data that consist of labels or nonnumerical categories are called ___ data.
hints: Examples: eye color, types of cars.

questions.prompt: What type of graph is best for showing qualitative data as parts of a whole?
hints: It's round and divided into slices.
Each slice represents a category's proportion.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A circle graph (pie chart) is best for showing parts of a whole.

questions.prompt: Are the budgets of feature films qualitative or quantitative?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Budgets are numerical measurements, so they are quantitative.

questions.prompt: Which graph is most appropriate for showing the distribution of test scores in a class?
hints: You want to see how scores are spread across intervals.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A histogram shows the frequency distribution of quantitative data.

questions.prompt: A graph that exaggerates or distorts the data by not starting the scale at zero or using uneven increments is called a ___ graph.
Why does a vertical scale starting above zero make a bar graph misleading?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: It makes differences appear larger than they really are.

questions.prompt: Which type of graph is best for showing how a quantity changes over time?
hints: It connects data points with a continuous line.
Used for trends across years, months, etc.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A line graph is best for showing change over time.

questions.prompt: To compare the distributions of two quantitative data sets side-by-side, a ___ box-and-whisker plot is often used.
hints: It has two sets of boxes and whiskers on the same scale.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A double box-and-whisker plot is used.

questions.prompt: Name one question you should ask to determine if a graph might be misleading.
questions.answer: Does the scale start at zero?
hints: Look at the numbers on the vertical scale.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Check if the scale starts at zero, if increments are even, or if labels are present.

questions.prompt: You want to display the favorite sports of students in your class. Which graph is most appropriate?
hints: Favorite sports are categories, not numbers.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A bar graph is best for comparing counts of qualitative categories.

questions.prompt: A circle graph displays data as parts of a whole. To find the angle for each category, multiply the fraction of the total by ___ degrees.
hints: A full circle has this many degrees.
The total angle in a circle.

questions.prompt: Give an example of data that is qualitative even though it uses numbers.
hints: Think of numbers used as labels.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Examples include telephone numbers, zip codes, jersey numbers, or street addresses.

questions.prompt: A graph of annual sales shows a vertical axis from 99.5 to 104.5 million dollars. Why is this misleading?
options: The scale does not start at zero
The years are not in order
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The scale does not start at zero, which exaggerates the increase.

questions.prompt: When choosing a data display, the first step is to classify the data as ___ or quantitative.
hints: Data that are labels or categories.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Classify the data as qualitative or quantitative.
